LESSON: SCHOOL AND COMMUNITY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People, Population and Social Organizations
Topic 2.4: School and Community
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers School and Community, part of People, Population and Social Organizations in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: which the school collaborates with the community. 1.How does the school collaborate with the community?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on School and Community together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self- efficacy: A learner acquires intrinsic self-motivation as they role-play ways in which the school

collaborates with the community.

● Citizenship: A learner develops information and communication skills as they act out scenarios that depict

collaboration between the school and the community.

Values:
• Integrity: A learner role-plays ways in which the school collaborates with the community.

29

• Social justice: A learner explains the benefits of collaboration between the school and the community.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Negotiation: A learner demonstrates ways in which the school collaborates with the community.

● Leadership: A learner shares experiences and benefits of school collaboration with the community.

Links to other Learning Areas:
• Learners write an essay on the benefits of collaboration between the school and the community enhancing their

knowledge in language skills such as English, Kiswahili and KSL.

• Learners use Creative Arts to role-play ways in which the school collaborates with the community.

Suggested Learning Resources:

School, local community, audio-visual clips, digital devices with assistive technology, approved appropriate print or

braille social studies textbooks and other relevant print or braille resources.
